landing.title: Discover which bird is singing near you in seconds with Artificial Intelligence
landing.subtitle: A citizen-science and ecological monitoring tool for biologists, park rangers, and nature enthusiasts. Instant acoustic identification from songs, calls, and trills in the open field.

how.title: From a murmur in the foliage to taxonomic certainty
how.step1Body: Capture directly with your phone's microphone, or upload WAV and MP3 files. Works even without mobile data.
how.step2Body: The model decomposes harmonics, center frequencies, and vocal cadence in under a second.
how.step3Body: Save your findings, explore distribution maps, and feed the collective biodiversity atlas.

offline.title: Built for the rigor of fieldwork
offline.body: Works fully offline in the rainforest, ravines, or high mountains. Your recordings are stored securely on your device and sync as soon as you regain coverage.

register.title: Join the Bioacoustics & Conservation Network
register.subtitle: Monitor bioindicators, sync field recordings with taxonomic AI, and collaborate on the planetary acoustic map.
register.consentScience: Share anonymized bioacoustic data with the global biodiversity network (GBIF/eBird).
register.consentTerms: I accept the Ethical Conservation Terms and the Bioacoustic Data Policy.

login.title: Welcome back to the field
login.subtitle: Sign in to sync your recordings and access your bioacoustic notebook.
login.remember: Keep session active on this device
login.orGateway: Or sign in with a scientific gateway

recording.micPermissionBody: Microphone permission is required. If the browser blocks it, check the lock icon in the address bar.
recording.fieldTipBody: Aim toward the mid-to-upper canopy layer and avoid crosswind gusts to keep harmonics above the noise floor.
